audience_question: What does the pilot evidence support the steering group doing next?
fit_rationale: The only plot-level fact supplied is the count of 12 positive and 6 not-positive plots out of 18, which is a whole-and-parts relationship; a grid of 18 squares keeps that denominator visible. Per-plot values are not supplied beyond the range, so a dot or bar plot would invent positions, and the median and range stay as text. The decision itself is stated in text because the evidence is summary statistics rather than a series or a comparison.
tradeoff: The square grid shows the count of positive plots but not their magnitudes, so the slide relies on the text for the +6% median and the −3% to +14% range; a reader who scans only the grid sees 12 of 18 without the size of the differences.
caveats: Pilot of 18 greenhouse plots at three sites over one winter growing cycle
Median yield difference +6% versus each site's reference plots; individual plot differences ranged from −3% to +14%
12 of 18 plots had a positive yield difference; 6 did not
Plots were not randomly assigned; crop mix and baseline conditions differed between sites
The pilot does not show that lighting caused the observed yield differences
Installation cost and energy use were not measured
Wider installation has not been approved; yield alone does not support it
Fictional scenario; all figures are invented for this evaluation
